newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Saudi exile in Afghanistan leaves Jalalabad.
newsitem.headline: Saudi exile in Afghanistan leaves Jalalabad.

text.p: Exiled Saudi Arabian dissident Osama bin Laden has left Afghanistan's eastern city of Jalalabad, where he has been living, for an unknown destination, an Afghan news service said on Saturday.

The private Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP), quoting sources in Jalalabad, said the Taleban Islamic movement flew Bin Laden and his supporters on Thursday to an unknown area, probably still in Afghanistan.
AIP said Bin Laden had been told by the Taleban not to give press interviews and issue statements against Saudi Arabia.

Bin Laden, named by the United States as a prime suspect in two bombings in Saudi Arabia that killed 24 U.S. servicemen and two Indians in 1995 and 1996, has lived in Afghanistan after he was forced to leave Sudan under Saudi pressure last year.
Bin Laden, a multi-millionaire financier stripped of his Saudi citizenship, has threatened to wage a holy war on U.S. forces in the homeland of Islam.
The Taleban, which controls more than two thirds of Afghanistan, says it will not allow the war-shattered country to be used for activities against any other nation.
